extracted.intended_audience: diagnostic assay developers, translational researchers, and grant reviewers (developers of lateral flow immunoassays for infectious disease)
extracted.subtask_description: Develop, optimize, manufacture, and validate a lateral flow immunoassay (LFI) to detect the capsular polysaccharide (CPS) of Burkholderia pseudomallei across relevant clinical matrices, and prepare for regulatory submission and pre-clinical evaluation at endemic sites.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation / novelty and public health impact
rubrics_metrics.description: A new addition to the diagnostic algorithm for melioidosis; AMD LFI designed to offer a significant improvement over current rapid techniques.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LFIs should be inexpensive, rapid, sensitive, stable at room temperature, not require expensive equipment, and accept multiple sample matrices to be useful in resource-poor settings. The InMAD platform is an innovative approach to identify circulating microbial biomarkers (e.g., CPS) and validation that CPS is shed into patient samples supports assay novelty and translational potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antibody selection: subclass and self-association
rubrics_metrics.description: IgG3 antibodies may not be ideal for LFI applications due to their ability to self-associate; self-association produced false positives and labeling difficulties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid IgG3 as both gold-labeled and test-line mAbs where self-association causes background. If IgG3 is present, consider isolating subclass switch variants (IgG1, IgG2a, IgG2b) though these may have altered affinity. Use SPR to detect self-association and evaluate subclass behavior during design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antibody selection: affinity and functional performance (KD, ELISA, LFI)
rubrics_metrics.description: mAbs should be characterized for binding affinity (KD) and performance by ELISA and LFI; higher affinity and appropriate subclass improve LFI performance (e.g., 4C4 IgG1 KD=12 nM improved LOD vs 3C5 IgG3 KD=73 nM).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure KD via SPR (biotinylated CPS on streptavidin chip), compare lots, and test as both gold conjugate and test-line mAb in multiple pairings to find best-performing combination. Consider that identical variable regions but different subclasses can yield different apparent affinities due to avidity/self-association.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit of Detection (LOD) definition and determination
rubrics_metrics.description: LOD is the concentration of CPS that yields a positive result 50% of the time and a negative result 50% of the time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow CLSI User Protocol for Evaluation for Qualitative Test Performance. Determine LOD on GMP-produced LFIs with sufficient replicates, across sample matrices (blood, serum, urine), and at collaborating sites as needed. Report LOD per sample matrix.

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical reactivity and specificity (panel testing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess reactivity to panels of B. pseudomallei, B. mallei, near-neighbor Burkholderia species, and common clinical bacteria to establish analytical sensitivity and specificity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use large, well-characterized panels (example: 77 B. pseudomallei, 33 B. mallei, 36 near neighbors from DHS/CDC panels). Expect high reactivity to B. pseudomallei, possible cross-reactivity with B. mallei where CPS is identical, and negative results for unrelated species. Use multiple colonies per isolate and verify discordant results via sequencing where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility / precision across sites
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess reproducibility of optimized LFI lots across multiple sites and concentrations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform reproducibility studies at three sites using Deki Readers for quantification and follow CLSI EP15-A2 (User Verification of Performance for Precision and Trueness). Include replicates at different agent concentrations and across different lots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interference and stability analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate interference (matrix effects, reagents, human antibodies) and stability of LFIs and components over time and storage conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct interference studies (e.g., pH variations in urine, anticoagulants in blood), accelerated and real-time stability testing on GMP lots, and document results in accordance with design control and regulatory expectations prior to shipping to collaborators.

rubrics_metrics.name: GMP production and design control compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce LFIs under documented design control and Good Manufacturing Practice (GMP) to ensure consistent manufacturing and traceability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish validated critical processes, training for operators, deviation handling, batch records to trace complete history, and ensure manufacturing staff trained for GMP. Produce multiple validated lots before large preclinical evaluation (target quantities specified).

rubrics_metrics.name: mAb purification QC
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality control steps for monoclonal antibody batches: non-denaturing Coomassie gel to check fragmentation, ELISA for binding to purified CPS, and SPR for KD determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare each lot to previous lots to ensure no variation in purity or binding. Purify via protein-A affinity chromatography and concentration; perform QC prior to use in labeling or LFI production.

rubrics_metrics.name: CPS purification and identity/purity verification
rubrics_metrics.description: Purify CPS (capsular polysaccharide) and verify structure and purity; use O-antigen-deficient strain to avoid LPS co-purification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Isolate CPS (e.g., modified hot aqueous-phenol procedure), verify structure/purity via Complex Carbohydrate Center or equivalent, and produce CPS under GLP for use as QC reagent in assay validation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample preparation protocols per matrix
rubrics_metrics.description: Standardized sample preparation guidelines for whole blood, serum, plasma, urine (concentrated and straight), pus, sputum (viscous and non-viscous), and bacterial colonies (Table 4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow optimized steps (sample volumes, centrifugation, lysis buffer, chase buffer additions) to maximize LFI sensitivity and consistency. Example: whole blood/serum/plasma combine 35 µl with 3 drops chase buffer; urine straight combine 50 µl with 3 drops chase buffer; sputum viscous combine 20 µl with 3 drops lysis buffer then add 20 µl lysate to sample pad followed by 3 drops chase buffer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample matrix compatibility and migration behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: The LFI must accept and perform across multiple clinical matrices (blood, serum, urine, sputum, pus, CSF, culture broth) and handle issues like sputum viscosity and erythrocyte removal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design sample pad and buffers to handle whole blood, filter erythrocytes, and enable flow for viscous specimens. Optimize migration (dilutions, lysis) to avoid incomplete migration or false negatives; validate performance with archived and spiked patient samples in endemic settings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample volume optimization and trade-offs
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine optimal sample volumes (typically 10–100 µl) balancing analyte concentration needs against background/false positives caused by higher volumes (e.g., pH effects).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Test multiple sample volumes per matrix. Increasing volume can improve sensitivity for low-analyte matrices but may increase false positives (observed with IgG3 interactions and pH variability). Use HAMA blockers and non-IgG3 mAbs to enable higher volumes when needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chase buffer function and formulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Chase buffer must (i) buffer all sample types (particularly urine with variable pH) and (ii) enhance product shelf life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formulate chase buffer to neutralize sample pH variations that cause false positives, support consistent flow, and prolong reagent stability. Evaluate in combination with sample pad and other components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conjugate pad and label stability/release
rubrics_metrics.description: Conjugate pad must stabilize the gold-labeled mAb over shelf life and consistently release conjugate to avoid assay variation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Labeling typically uses colloidal gold; evaluate other labels (latex, europium) for sensitivity. Optimize labeling efficiency (label diameter, method) and pad treatments to ensure stable long-term performance and consistent conjugate release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membrane selection (nitrocellulose) and treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Select nitrocellulose membranes based on pore size, flow rate, and lot-to-lot consistency; membranes must be converted to hydrophilic via surfactant treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Screen membranes from multiple suppliers for flow characteristics and consistency. Choose membrane that supports desired flow rate to optimize sensitivity and assay time, and validate hydrophilicity treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Test-line mAb pairing strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Using the same mAb for conjugate and test line is permissible because CPS has repeating epitopes, but using different mAbs targeting different epitopes may improve sensitivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Experiment with combinations (conjugate vs test-line mAbs) to identify best-performing pairings. Test both same-mAb and heterologous pairs during prototype optimization and measure LOD and background.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absorbent pad sizing and composition
rubrics_metrics.description: Absorbent pad serves as a sink for processed liquid; size and composition should be adjusted based on required sample volume to reach sensitivity targets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match absorbent pad capacity to sample volume and flow characteristics determined during LOD and matrix testing. Larger sample volumes may require larger sink capacity to maintain flow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mitigation of HAMA and other human antibody effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Human anti-mouse antibody (HAMA) reactions can bind gold-labeled mouse mAb and test-line mAb producing false positives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Incorporate commercially available HAMA blockers into the sample pad formulation and evaluate their effectiveness. Also consider switching to non-mouse or engineered antibodies to reduce HAMA interference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital reader implementation and data capture (Deki Reader)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use Deki Reader to scan LFIs, quantify test/control line intensity, and store test results in a secure cloud network (Fionet).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement Deki Readers at testing sites to improve interpretation consistency, enable quantitative comparisons across sites and lots, and facilitate reproducibility studies and remote data aggregation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory planning and 510(k) pre-submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek pre-submission guidance from FDA to define required studies for 510(k) submission and clarify regulatory expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage industry experience (InBios history of approved diagnostics) to lead interactions with FDA, identify relevant guidance documents, and design validation studies (archival vs prospective) required for 510(k).

rubrics_metrics.name: Benchmarks, timelines, and production scale targets
rubrics_metrics.description: Define timeline and measurable benchmarks for success: finalize components by mid Project Year 2, complete endemic site evaluation by end Project Year 2, produce specified reagent quantities and LFI lots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Targets include producing 100 mg purified CPS and 1 g mAb 4C4 by end of Year 2, and producing ~5000 GMP 4C4 AMD LFIs for large preclinical analysis in Project Year 3. Success metrics: i) finalized optimized LFI components, ii) validated sample preparation guidelines, iii) 4C4 LFI with improved performance over 3C5 LFI, and clarity on data needed for 510(k).

rubrics_metrics.name: Analytical testing workflow and endemic-site validation
rubrics_metrics.description: Spike purified CPS into control and patient sample matrices, provide prototypes to collaborators in endemic countries, and test archived/clinical specimens including culture broth and blood culture bottles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ship batches (e.g., 50 LFIs initially, then more) to collaborators in Thailand, Australia, Laos for evaluation using standardized sample prep. Include studies to evaluate earlier detection from culture broths, spiked blood cultures, and archived febrile illness samples; use results to iterate on LFI components and protocols.
